verdicts.reason: Strongest point of X is the witness-flip rule that blocks rigged checks plus a 10-brief test with kill criteria and an ambition guard, whereas Y's strongest point is atomic-claim grounding (Min 2023) but its one-brief test cannot measure preference over the single agent; X's test fits the benchmark better.

X adds load-bearing flags that penalise claim-weakening and a 10-brief blinded panel test with kill thresholds against the single agent, while Y (strongest point: a clean bounded loop with template library) tests on one brief and leaves triviality-weakening only diagnosed, not penalised.

X adds codebase probes so this qualitative brief still has checkable feasibility claims, a step-0 checkable-fraction kill test, and median-s for sparse cards instead of last place, whereas Y (strongest point: simple ledger scoring) admits it mostly yields not_checkable and s~0 for such briefs.

X is standalone on finalists with a 1.4x token cap, revert-to-original floor and an offline test on saved cards that can run in the existing benchmark, while Y (strongest point: full 3-iteration loop) depends on an assumed ledger and costs 2x tokens, making it harder to test and compare at equal cost.
